51494482.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to Helicobacter pyroli urease assessed as dissociation constant by surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.Results_section_text: The most active compound (d7) was selected for inhibition mechanism exploration. The surface plasmon resonance assay (Fig. 3A) revealed sub-nanomolar level of Kd (0.34 nM), suggesting the excellent binding affinity of d7 to urease. The enzyme kinetic assay performed on microplate reader (Fig. 4) disclosed that d7 inhibits urease in a mixed
original_paragraph.Figure_3_caption: Fig. 3. A: SPR profile of compound d7.
original_paragraph.Figure_3_A_plot_labels: Concentrations: 2.07 μg/mL, 12.5 μg/mL, 15.625 μg/mL. X-axis: Time (s) from 0 to 500. Y-axis: Signal (arbitrary units) from 0 to 120.
original_paragraph.Figure_3_B_plot_labels: X-axis: Time (min) from 0 to 120. Y-axis: Inhibition (%) from 0 to 100. Data points show inhibition increasing over time, reaching ~95% at 120 min.
original_paragraph.Text_discussing_Fig_3_B: Fig. 3B: The effect of incubation time on inhibition of d7 (100 μg/mL) against urease. Each point represents the average of triplicate incubations.
original_paragraph.Text_discussing_Kd_value: mechanism with Ki value of 0.065 ± 0.003 μM and Ki' value of 1.20 ± 0.09 μM, respectively, Ki is the dissociation constant for “enzyme-inhibitor → enzyme (E) and inhibitor”, and Ki' is the dissociation constant for “enzyme-substrate-inhibitor → enzyme-substrate (ES) and inhibitor”, which also means the affinity of ligand to urease. Fig. 3B disclosed that d7 inhibited urease in a time dependent manner, indicating that 50 mins are required for the maximum inhibition.
